You are a regulatory-genomics analyst QC'ing a cross-species enhancer-activity table before an activity/conservation analysis. You are given a raw cross-species enhancer-activity table (a STARR-seq screen), delivered as an Excel (.xlsx) workbook that may or may not contain data-integrity / QC problems. Determine whether these enhancer activity rows (coordinates + sequences) can be TRUSTED for downstream regulatory analysis (predicting enhancer activity from sequence, and comparing enhancer activity vs sequence conservation across species), and what would need to be fixed first.

Dataset path: /tmp/gwsbx_plw01vhd/cell005.xlsx   (an .xlsx workbook — the ORIGINAL Klein-2018 Supplementary File 2 format)
The enhancer table is on sheet 'S4 All ortholog scores'. In that sheet ROW 0 is a title ('Table S4. Ortholog Scores'), ROW 1 is the real header (['Enhancer Coordinates (hg19)', 'Enrichment Score', 'sequence']), and the data start at ROW 2 — so read it with e.g. pandas.read_excel(path, sheet_name='S4 All ortholog scores', header=1) (openpyxl is installed).
Each row is one species ORTHOLOG of an enhancer. The coordinate is a STRING '<chrom>:<start>-<end>_<assembly>' (0-based half-open; <assembly> = the ortholog genome, e.g. hg38, panTro5, gorGor3, ponAbe2, macFas5, rheMac3, papAnu2, chlSab2, calJac3, nomLeu3, saiBol1) — parse chrom/start/end/assembly out of it yourself. 'Enrichment Score' is log2 enhancer activity; 'sequence' is the forward (+) strand DNA fetched for that coordinate. Its directory may contain additional files.

A read-only reference is available (mounted at this absolute path):
  - /workspace/discern-benchmark/tracks/enhancer_activity/data/resources/hg38_reference_loci.tsv   (tab-separated: coordinate<TAB>sequence — the forward (+) strand reference sequence for the HUMAN (hg38) enhancer loci; use it to check sequence integrity / orientation for hg38 rows).

You have a Python sandbox: call run_python(code). Parse the .xlsx yourself with pandas.read_excel / openpyxl (pandas as pd, numpy as np, scipy.stats as stats; sklearn/pysam importable); you may also read the reference file above and any other files in the dataset's directory. Only text you print is returned; plots are NOT rendered.

Record EVERY check you run in `trajectory` (including checks that turned up nothing). Then return ONLY this JSON:
{"issues_found": [{"description": "<what is wrong, in your words, or 'none'>",
                    "affected_entities": ["<id / coordinate / column, if identifiable>"],
